It's a landscape defining happening in the sci fi landscape. I am quite amazed you didn't know what it was. It's not about the reviews. It's about who holds the power and dictates what people get to write about, if they don't want to be black balled from the industry.

Well, that's the thing. I wasn't really part of the community before. That's changing now, but before I just didn't pay attention to the larger community. It's...difficult to really explain what I'm getting from reading up on all this. I agree with their stated intention, which is that authors shouldn't necessarily be rewarded for pushing an ideology, but rather whether their books are actually well made or not. That being said, it seems like what they're actually doing is trying to take the teeth out of sci-fi: you can have your spaceship battles and laser fights, but if you start trying to actually make a point with those spaceships you're doing it wrong. I guess if I was put to it, I'd say I'm against it, but I just feel like since I haven't really been involved I don't have much of a say one way or the other.

Science fiction has always been an allegory for how things are. I don't think that is likely to change. It seems to me that the blow back — in the form of * Puppies — is about having a social inquisition about media. I'd prefer that non interested parties, that is, ppl who aren't fans, not get a vote.

the legends tell you why the stone heads lie at the edge of the hot brine basin, just a bit farther north of the obelisk volcano. obelisk wasn't always empty, save for a few villages that worshiped the volcano's god. there used to be great cities, you can still find ruins if you look. things, emerged from the brine. towering and a mans shape, and adorned in vibrant colors over forms fit for fine statues.

their name used to be known, now, no longer. they tore the cities into pieces at their leisure. thousands of years of gold and scholars ended, under a giants foot. sometimes the cities mounted an unsuccessful defense, but the giants would stay at their attacks, making chairs and thrones of stone towers. stomping and herding survivors into pits they dug by monstrous hand, and snacked as they wanted. half the volcano was rubble when the first followers emerged.

they begged for a salvation, they invented new names, new altars, new rituals. trying to call something from the endless wastes around them. for a year and a day, the high priests chanted dressed in obsidian pendants, and obsidian crowns. tossing spices into fire, and watching the flames flare green and blue and purple. and when they thought it was all in vain, something answered, from deep below their feet.
